name: Subsets of {1, ..., 200} in which square products of four elements force ad = bc
description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..200 such that whenever a <= b <= c <= d are elements (repetition allowed) with abcd a perfect square, ad = bc (checked exactly through parity vectors of prime exponents). Maximize the size; the optimum is 102. For n = 200 the maximum is 102, so the task recovers an extremal set.

sources.locator: Paul Erdős, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number theory (1998). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #888 page inspected (a question of Erdős, Sárközy and Sós; |A| = o(n); primes and semiprimes give (1+o(1)) n log log n/log n, and a matching upper bound was proved recently and verified in Lean). OEIS A387584 inspected (b-file by Sievers for n <= 203): the maximum for n = 200 is 102, attained by the primes together with the products of two distinct primes. For n = 200 the maximum is 102, so the task recovers an extremal set.
